docs.title: vexy-stax-js
docs.text:
vexy-stax-js draws a stack of images as a deck of 3D glass plates in the browser. It reads the vexy-stax scene format, the same JSON file that the Python package vexy-stax-py renders, and shows the deck in two views:

  • expanded: the plates stand apart, seen from an angle, so each layer is visible on its own;
  • compact: the plates close up into one flat picture, seen head-on.

The deck can morph between the two views as an animation, on a click, or as the page scrolls. It can export the current view as a PNG image and the transition as a video. Rendering uses three.js.

docs.title: Three ways to use it
Live demos

The demos are described in Live demos.

docs.title: ESM API
docs.text:
Import the API from the element bundle, or from the npm package when you use a bundler:

import { createStax, VexyStax, loadScene, makeScene, parseScene }
  from "https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.element.js";

// or, with npm and a bundler
import { createStax, VexyStax, loadScene, makeScene, parseScene } from "vexy-stax-js";

The global bundle exposes VexyStax, createStax, loadScene, makeScene and create (an alias of createStax) on window.VexyStax.

docs.title: createStax
docs.text:
const stax = await createStax(elOrSelector, opts);

createStax is the shortest way to a working deck. It:

  1. finds the mount element (an element or a CSS selector) and throws createStax: element not found (…) if there is none;
  2. applies width, height and aspect to the element's style;
  3. builds the scene: from slides with makeScene, or from scene with loadScene;
  4. overrides the scene's view with view, if given;
  5. creates a VexyStax and waits for ready;
  6. starts the mode: playable plays the scene's transition once (if the scene has one); scrollspy attaches scroll tracking to trigger;
  7. turns on click-to-toggle unless clickToggle is false;
  8. adds control buttons if buttons is set.

It resolves with the ready VexyStax instance.

const stax = await createStax("#stage", {
  slides: ["layer-0.png", "layer-1.png"],
  gap: 480,
  transition: "expand_collapse",
  mode: "playable",
});

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Key Type Default Effect slides string[] or slide objects — Images, back to front. Takes precedence over scene. scene URL string or scene object — Used when slides is absent view "expanded" or "compact" the scene's view Initial view mode "static", "playable" or "scrollspy" "static" Start mode trigger element or CSS selector the mount element Scroll trigger for scrollspy width, height CSS length; a bare number means pixels — Element size aspect number or string such as "3/1" — CSS aspect-ratio of the element clickToggle boolean true false turns click-to-toggle off baseUrl string document.baseURI Base for relative slide and scene URLs buttons true, "toggle", "pair" or an options object — Control buttons; see controls explainLabel, previewLabel string "Explain", "Preview" Button labels buttonsPosition string "bottom" Button position buttonStyle string — Extra inline CSS for the button bar

When slides is given, every other key that is not in the table above except the button keys is passed to makeScene as a scene override: size, camera, gap, transition, background, captions, floor, edge, juicy, caption_defaults, caption_fade and video.

Buttons with slides

In version 3.1.9 the button keys (buttons, explainLabel, previewLabel, buttonsPosition, buttonStyle) are also forwarded to makeScene, which rejects them with makeScene: unknown option "buttons". With slides, call stax.controls() after createStax instead. With scene, the button keys work.

docs.title: VexyStax
docs.text:
The class behind the element and createStax.

const scene = await loadScene("deck.scene.json");
const stax = new VexyStax(document.querySelector("#stage"), scene);
await stax.ready;

new VexyStax(container, scene) needs a mount element and a parsed scene (from loadScene, parseScene or makeScene). It throws VexyStax: container is required or VexyStax: scene must be a parsed scene object (use loadScene first) otherwise. The constructor adds a canvas to the container and starts loading the slide textures.

docs.title: ready
docs.text: stax.ready is a promise that resolves to the instance once the textures are loaded and the first frame is drawn. The render methods wait for it themselves.

docs.title: toImage({ scale })
docs.text:
const blob = await stax.toImage({ scale: 2 });

Renders the current frame and returns it as a PNG Blob. With scale other than 1, it renders once at that multiple of the current pixel ratio, then restores the canvas. Remote images must be served with CORS headers, or the canvas cannot be exported.

docs.title: toVideo(opts)
docs.text:
const blob = await stax.toVideo();
const blob2 = await stax.toVideo({ kind: "expand" });

Records a clip of the transition and returns it as a Blob. The clip has three parts: the start frame repeated video.first_hold times (default 10), the animated transition, and the end frame repeated video.last_hold times (default 10). The frame rate is video.fps, else transition.fps, else 30.

opts.kind overrides the scene's transition kind. Without a kind in either place, the method throws.

The encoder is chosen automatically:

  1. WebCodecs: when VideoEncoder exists, frames are encoded one by one as H.264 (or VP9 when the browser cannot encode H.264) and muxed with mp4-muxer. The file has correct duration metadata and can be seeked.
  2. MediaRecorder: otherwise the canvas stream is recorded live with the first supported type among VP9, VP8, WebM and MP4. The result may lack duration metadata.

docs.title: transition(kind, opts)
docs.text:
await stax.transition();
await stax.transition("expand", { onProgress: (p) => console.log(p) });

Plays a transition as an animation and resolves when it ends. kind is one of expand, collapse, expand_collapse and collapse_expand; it defaults to the scene's transition.kind. Without either, the method throws.

Option Type Effect onProgress (p) => void Called each frame with the overall progress from 0 to 1 duration number (seconds) Overrides the scene's transition.duration

The container receives transitionstart and transitionend events, each with detail.kind.

docs.title: scrollspy(opts)
docs.text:
const handle = stax.scrollspy({ trigger: "#story", kind: "expand" });
// later
handle.disconnect();

Drives the morph from the scroll position of a trigger element. An IntersectionObserver starts the scroll tracking only while the trigger is visible. The scroll progress from 0 to 1 goes through the same timeline as the animation (including the wait hold), unless you pass map.

Option Type Default Effect trigger element or CSS selector — Required. Throws VexyStax.scrollspy: trigger element not found if missing. kind string scene transition kind, else expand Timeline to follow reducedMotion boolean the prefers-reduced-motion setting When true, the deck snaps between compact and expanded instead of morphing map (p) => t — Your own mapping from scroll progress to morph factor; the result is clamped to 0–1

It returns { disconnect() }. Calling scrollspy again replaces the previous tracking.

docs.title: controls(opts)
docs.text:
stax.controls({ type: "pair", explainLabel: "Open", previewLabel: "Close", position: "top-right" });
stax.controls(false); // remove the buttons

Adds buttons over the deck and replaces any previous ones.

Option Values Default type "toggle" (one button whose label follows the view) or "pair" "toggle" explainLabel text of the expand action "Explain" previewLabel text of the collapse action "Preview" position bottom, top, bottom-left, bottom-right, top-left, top-right, center bottom style extra inline CSS for the button bar —

The buttons are themed with --vexy-btn-* custom properties; see Web Component.

docs.title: Other instance methods
docs.text: Method Effect setView(view) Renders the compact or expanded view without animation. Resolves with the instance. seek(t) Renders the morph at t (0 = compact, 1 = expanded, clamped). Emits viewchange when t crosses 0.5. toggleView() Animates to the other view in 0.7 seconds and resolves with the kind it played ("expand" or "collapse"), or null if a toggle was already running enableClickToggle() Calls toggleView() on clicks inside the container, except on buttons, links and form fields disableClickToggle() Removes that click handler resize(width, height) Resizes the renderer and camera; without arguments it uses the container size destroy() Stops animations and scroll tracking, removes buttons and the click handler, and disposes of the three.js stage

docs.title: loadScene(urlOrObject, options)
docs.text:
const a = await loadScene("deck.scene.json");
const b = await loadScene("deck.scene.json", { baseUrl: "https://example.com/decks/" });
const c = await loadScene({ version: 1, slides: [{ src: "a.png" }] });

With a string, fetches the JSON (relative to options.baseUrl or the page) and throws Failed to fetch scene <url>: <status> on an HTTP error. With an object, uses it directly. In both cases it runs parseScene and then resolves each slide's src against the scene URL or baseUrl. data: URIs are kept as they are.

docs.title: makeScene(slides, opts)
docs.text:
const scene = makeScene(["a.png", "b.png"], { gap: 480, transition: "expand_collapse" });

Builds a parsed scene from a list of image URLs or slide objects ({ src, caption, opacity, gap }). Options:

  • baseUrl resolves relative slide URLs;
  • gap is a shortcut for camera.gap;
  • transition may be a kind string, which becomes { kind: "…" };
  • size, camera, view, background, captions, floor, edge, juicy, caption_defaults, caption_fade and video map to the scene fields of the same name.

Any other option throws makeScene: unknown option "…". An empty slide list throws too.

docs.title: parseScene(raw)
docs.text:
Validates a raw scene object, fills in the defaults and returns the normalized scene. It rejects anything the schema does not allow, with messages such as:

slides is required
version must be 1 (got 2)
Unknown key "bogus" in scene
slides[0].opacity must be <= 1
transition.kind must be one of expand, collapse, expand_collapse, collapse_expand (got "spin")

docs.title: Lower-level exports
docs.text:
src/index.js also exports the pure functions that the renderer is built on. They have no DOM dependencies and are covered by the unit tests:

  • geometry: MIN_GAP, FILL, plateGaps, stackDepth, compactCamera, expandedCamera, ease, interpolateOpacity, framePlan, frameStateAt;
  • timing: buildTimeline, morphAtProgress, transitionEndpoints;
  • scroll: computeScrollProgress, prefersReducedMotion;
  • scene: resolvedOpacity;
  • export: canvasToPngBlob.

These are exported from the npm entry (src/index.js), not from the element bundle.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page explains how vexy-stax-js turns a scene into frames, and where each part lives in the source.

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text:
src/
├── index.js       public ESM API: VexyStax class and createStax
├── element.js     <vexy-stax> custom element; registers itself on import
├── global.js      entry of the classic-script bundle (window.VexyStax)
├── scene.js       scene parser and validator, makeScene, loadScene
├── geometry.js    view math: plate gaps, stack depth, cameras, easing, frame states
├── stage.js       three.js scene: plates, captions, floor, reflections, camera
├── transition.js  timeline of a transition and the requestAnimationFrame driver
├── scrollspy.js   scroll position → progress, with reduced-motion handling
├── controls.js    the Explain / Preview buttons
└── export.js      PNG export and video recording
schema/            JSON Schema of the scene format
demo-scenes/       editable scene files for the live demos
scripts/           build-docs.mjs, which writes the live demos
tests/             node --test unit tests and Playwright end-to-end tests
verify/            render checks that fail on blank output
src_docs/          this documentation site (ProperDocs)

vite.config.js builds two bundles from two entries: src/element.js as an ES module (dist/vexy-stax.element.js) and src/global.js as an IIFE (dist/vexy-stax.global.js). Each bundle includes three.js and mp4-muxer.

docs.title: From scene to frame
docs.text: Take a scene with three slides, the default camera.gap of 1920 and the expand transition, mounted in the compact view.

docs.title: 1. Parsing
docs.text: parseScene checks the raw object against the scene rules and fills in every default, so later code never sees a missing field. loadScene then resolves each slide's src to an absolute URL. The result is a plain object.

docs.title: 2. Geometry
docs.text:
geometry.js computes everything about a view as numbers, without three.js:

  • Gaps. In the expanded view, the space in front of each plate is the slide's own gap or camera.gap (1920 here). In the compact view every gap becomes MIN_GAP (3 scene units), so the plates almost touch.
  • Depth. The front plate sits at Z = 0 and the backmost (slide 0) at Z = −depth. With three slides the expanded depth is 2 × 1920 = 3840 and the compact depth is 2 × 3 = 6.
  • Cameras. compactCamera looks straight down the Z axis at the front slide and fits it to the frame. expandedCamera orbits by camera.angle degrees and rises by camera.elevation degrees, and fits the whole deck. A distance such as "100%" is solved from the field of view and the aspect ratio of the element.
  • Morph. frameStateAt(scene, t, aspect) mixes the two views for a morph factor t between 0 (compact) and 1 (expanded): camera pose, gaps, slide opacities and caption opacities.

The same formulas exist in vexy-stax-py. tests/geometry.test.js checks the JavaScript results against fixture values from the Python test suite.

docs.title: 3. Stage
docs.text: stage.js builds the three.js objects once: a textured plane per slide, an optional border, caption plates, a floor with reflections and a perspective camera. For each frame it applies a frame state (positions, opacities, camera) and renders it with the WebGL renderer.

docs.title: 4. Motion
docs.text:
Each transition kind is a list of legs between the two views:

Kind Legs expand compact → expanded collapse expanded → compact expand_collapse compact → expanded, then expanded → compact collapse_expand expanded → compact, then compact → expanded

buildTimeline lays the legs out in time: each leg moves for duration seconds and then holds its end view for wait seconds. With the defaults (3 and 1), expand_collapse lasts 8 seconds. Three drivers then move along the timeline:

  • transition() follows the clock with requestAnimationFrame;
  • scrollspy() follows the scroll position, via morphAtProgress;
  • toVideo() follows the clock while it records each frame, with held frames before and after.

In each case the driver computes t, asks frameStateAt for the state and renders it.

docs.title: Events and state
docs.text: VexyStax remembers the current view. setView, seek, transition and toggleView update it, and every change fires a viewchange event on the container. The buttons from controls.js listen to that event to update their labels.

docs.title: Building the documentation site
docs.text:
dist/ ─┐
demo-scenes/ ─┼─ scripts/build-docs.mjs ──> src_docs/md/  (demo pages, bundles, scenes, slides)
vexy-stax-py/testdata ─┘                       │
src_docs/md/*.md ──────────────────────────────┤
                                               └─ src_docs/build.sh (ProperDocs) ──> docs/

GitHub Pages serves docs/ from the main branch at https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/. The workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml rebuilds docs/ when src_docs/ changes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js 18 or later (.nvmrc pins 20) and npm
  • A checkout of vexy-stax-py next to this repository (../vexy-stax-py). The geometry tests and the demo build read its testdata/ folder.
  • For the documentation site: uv (provides uvx)
  • For the render checks: Python 3 with Pillow and NumPy

docs.title: Setting up
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-stax-js.git
cd vexy-stax-js
./install.sh

install.sh runs npm install and npx playwright install chromium.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does npm run dev Starts the Vite development server npm run build Builds dist/vexy-stax.element.js and dist/vexy-stax.global.js npm run test:unit Runs the node --test unit tests (scene, geometry, stage, transition) npm test Runs the unit tests, then the Playwright tests in tests/e2e/ npm run build:docs Writes the live demos into src_docs/md/ (needs dist/) ./build.sh Unit tests, bundles, demos, then the documentation site ./build.sh docs Only the documentation site, from src_docs/ into docs/ ./example.sh Renders sample PNGs, a video and scroll frames into outputs/ and checks them

The Playwright tests mount a deck, switch views, export an image, play a transition, record a video and drive the scroll mode in headless Chromium.

docs.title: Render checks
docs.text:
A WebGL bug can produce a canvas that is valid but empty. The verify/ scripts catch that:

node verify/run.mjs && python3 verify/gate.py

run.mjs serves the repository over HTTP, opens verify/harness.html in Chromium, renders the compact and expanded views and saves them as PNG files. gate.py fails unless each image has a pixel standard deviation above 30 and more than 500 distinct colours.

docs.title: Rebuilding the demos
docs.text:
The live demos are generated files. Their sources are:

  • the page templates in scripts/build-docs.mjs;
  • the bundles in dist/;
  • the scene files in demo-scenes/, which you can edit by hand;
  • the slide images in ../vexy-stax-py/testdata/airbl-lores/.

To rebuild them:

  1. Build the bundles: npm run build.
  2. Write the demos: npm run build:docs. The script writes demos.html, playable.html, scrollable.html and the three demo-*.html pages, and copies the bundles, scene files and slides, all into src_docs/md/.
  3. Build the site: ./build.sh docs.
  4. Serve docs/ and open the demos to check them, for example with python3 -m http.server --directory docs.

If ../vexy-stax-py is missing, step 2 keeps the slide images that are already in src_docs/md/airbl-lores/.

docs.title: Writing documentation
docs.text:
The pages are Markdown files in src_docs/md/. The navigation is the nav list in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

  1. Edit a page, or add one and list it in nav.

  2. Preview with live reload:

    src_docs/build.sh serve

    The preview runs at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

  3. Build in strict mode: ./build.sh docs. Any warning, such as a broken link between pages, fails the build.

Do not edit docs/ by hand. The build replaces its contents, and the .github/workflows/docs.yml workflow rebuilds it on every push to main that touches src_docs/.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Maintainers publish to npm with ./publish.sh. Without arguments it:

  1. tags the next version with uvx gitnextver;
  2. writes that version into package.json;
  3. builds and publishes the package with npm, running npm login first if needed.

./publish.sh --dryrun packs and checks the package without bumping the version or publishing.

The workflow .github/workflows/publish.yml also publishes to npm, with provenance, when a GitHub release is published.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
vexy-stax-js runs in the browser. It needs WebGL for rendering. Video export uses WebCodecs where the browser has it and falls back to MediaRecorder.

There are two ways to get it: load a prebuilt bundle with a <script> tag, or install the npm package and let your bundler include it.

docs.title: Prebuilt bundles
docs.text:
The build produces two self-contained bundles. three.js and the MP4 muxer are compiled in, so a page needs nothing else.

Bundle Format Provides vexy-stax.element.js ES module Registers <vexy-stax> and exports createStax, VexyStax, makeScene, loadScene, parseScene vexy-stax.global.js Classic script (IIFE) Registers <vexy-stax> and sets window.VexyStax

docs.title: Use the hosted copy
docs.text:
This site serves the current bundles next to the demos. GitHub Pages sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so other sites can load them:

<!-- Web Component and ES module -->
<script type="module" src="https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.element.js"></script>

<!-- Global script -->
<script src="https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.global.js"></script>

The hosted copy changes when the site is rebuilt. For a fixed version, copy the file into your own project.

docs.title: Build the bundles yourself
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Git and Node.js 18 or later (the repository's .nvmrc pins Node 20).

  1. Clone the repository and install the development dependencies:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-stax-js.git
cd vexy-stax-js
npm ci

  2. Build:

    npm run build

    Vite writes dist/vexy-stax.element.js and dist/vexy-stax.global.js, each with a source map.

  3. Copy the bundle you need into your site and load it with a <script> tag.

docs.title: npm package
docs.text:
npm install vexy-stax-js

The package's exports entry points to src/index.js, the unbundled ES module source, with three and mp4-muxer as dependencies. A bundler such as Vite, Rollup or webpack resolves them:

import { createStax, makeScene, VexyStax, loadScene } from "vexy-stax-js";

The src/index.js entry does not register the <vexy-stax> element, and the package's exports map exposes only that entry (and package.json). For the Web Component, load the prebuilt vexy-stax.element.js bundle.

jsDelivr URLs

The npm package ships src/ and schema/ but not dist/. URLs of the form https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-stax-js@<version>/dist/…, which the demo pages mention, return 404 for the published versions. Use the hosted copy above instead.

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text: The package includes schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json, a JSON Schema for scene files. Point your editor at it to get completion and validation while you write a scene. See Scene format.

docs.title: Browser requirements
docs.text: Feature Needed for WebGL All rendering (three.js WebGLRenderer) Custom elements <vexy-stax> ResizeObserver Refitting the camera when the element changes size IntersectionObserver Scroll-driven mode (mode="scrollspy") WebCodecs VideoEncoder Seekable MP4 or WebM export with toVideo() MediaRecorder The toVideo() fallback when WebCodecs is missing

docs.title: Live demos
docs.text:
The demos are static HTML pages published next to this documentation. Each page loads the bundle from the same folder (vexy-stax.element.js or vexy-stax.global.js), so it always runs the version this site was built with. The animated and scrollspy demos show an eight-layer artwork from airbl-lores/; the how-to pages use four of its layers.

Open the demo overview for a card for each demo and a set of copy-paste snippets.

docs.title: Animated demo
docs.text:
playable.html loads airbl-demo.scene.json into a <vexy-stax> element in the compact view. When the deck is ready, it plays the expand transition once. Three buttons control it:

  • Play transition calls el.transition("expand_collapse"): the deck opens and closes again.
  • Compact and Expanded call el.setView("compact") and el.setView("expanded"), which jump to that view without animation.

The page reads the scene's size and sets the element's CSS aspect-ratio to match it.

docs.title: Scrollspy demo
docs.text:
scrollable.html places the deck between two screen-high text sections. The element loads airbl-scrollable.scene.json in the compact view with buttons="toggle".

A page script maps the scroll position to the morph factor and calls el.seek(t):

  • t = 0 (compact) until 75% of the element's height is inside the window;
  • t rises with an ease-in-out curve as you scroll on;
  • t = 1 (expanded) once the element's centre reaches the top of the window.

A click on the deck plays a toggle animation. The page then keeps the clicked state until the scroll position reaches the same end point, so the deck does not jump back after a click.

docs.title: How-to pages
docs.text:
Each how-to page shows a short code sample on the left and the live result on the right.

demo-component.html shows the <vexy-stax> element:

  • a deck from the slides attribute;
  • captions on, in the expanded view;
  • a scene URL with mode="playable";
  • a whole scene inline in a <script type="application/json"> child;
  • a 3:1 box from aspect="3";
  • a built-in toggle button (buttons);
  • a pair of buttons with custom labels, position and --vexy-btn-* colours.

demo-module.html shows createStax from the ES module:

  • a deck from a list of slides;
  • a playable deck with a custom gap and transition kind;
  • an inline scene object, with no file to fetch;
  • click-to-toggle together with calls to the instance methods.

demo-library.html shows the global script and window.VexyStax.create.

CDN links on the demo pages

The how-to pages also print jsDelivr URLs for the bundles. Those URLs do not work for the current npm releases, because the npm package does not include dist/. Load the bundles from this site instead, as described in Installation.

docs.title: Where the demo files come from
docs.text: npm run build:docs runs scripts/build-docs.mjs. The script writes the demo pages, copies the two bundles and their source maps from dist/, copies the scene files from demo-scenes/ and the slide images from the sibling vexy-stax-py checkout, all into src_docs/md/. The documentation build then copies these files unchanged into docs/, so every demo keeps its URL. See Contributing.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page builds the same deck three ways. The deck has three layer images, layer-0.png, layer-1.png and layer-2.png, stored next to the HTML page. The first image in the list is the backmost plate; the last is the front.

Prerequisites: the images, and a local web server. Browsers do not load ES modules or WebGL textures from file:// pages, so serve the folder, for example with npx vite or python3 -m http.server.

docs.title: 1. With the Web Component
docs.text:
1. Create index.html:

    <!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <script type="module" src="https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.element.js"></script>
  </head>
  <body>
    <vexy-stax
      slides="layer-0.png layer-1.png layer-2.png"
      view="compact"
      aspect="16/9"
      buttons>
    </vexy-stax>
  </body>
</html>

  2. Open the page through your web server.

The element splits slides at spaces and newlines, builds a scene with default settings and renders the compact view in a 16:9 box. buttons adds an Explain button. Click it, or anywhere in the deck, and the plates move apart into the expanded view; the button now reads Preview and brings the deck back.

docs.title: 2. With the ES module
docs.text:
1. Replace the element with an empty container and a module script:

    <div id="stage" style="width: 800px; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9"></div>

<script type="module">
  import { createStax } from "https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.element.js";

  const stax = await createStax("#stage", {
    slides: ["layer-0.png", "layer-1.png", "layer-2.png"],
    transition: "expand_collapse",
    mode: "playable",
  });
</script>

  2. Reload the page.

createStax builds the scene, mounts the deck, waits until the textures are loaded and returns a VexyStax instance. With mode: "playable" it plays the scene's transition once: here expand_collapse, which opens the deck and closes it again. Clicking the deck still toggles the view.

The instance has the render methods. Add these lines to export the current view as a PNG and the transition as a video:

const png = await stax.toImage({ scale: 2 });
const video = await stax.toVideo();

Both return a Blob. See ESM API.

docs.title: 3. With the global script
docs.text:
For pages without modules, load the global bundle. It defines window.VexyStax:

<div id="stage" style="width: 800px; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9"></div>

<script src="https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.global.js"></script>
<script>
  VexyStax.create("#stage", { slides: ["layer-0.png", "layer-1.png", "layer-2.png"] });
</script>

VexyStax.create is the same function as createStax.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Write a scene file to set captions, spacing, camera angle, colours and transition timing, then load it with <vexy-stax scene="deck.scene.json">.
  • Make the deck follow the page scroll with mode="scrollspy"; see Web Component.
  • Try the live demos.

docs.title: Scene format
docs.text:
A vexy-stax scene is a JSON object that describes a deck: the slide images, the camera, the transition, captions and colours. The same file works in vexy-stax-js (the three.js renderer in the browser) and in vexy-stax-py, the Python package with its own render engines. Scene files usually end in .scene.json.

parseScene checks every scene strictly: unknown keys, wrong types, values out of range and unknown enum values are errors, not warnings. See ESM API.

The JSON Schema is schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json in the repository and in the npm package.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
{
  "version": 1,
  "slides": [
    { "src": "layer-0.png" },
    { "src": "layer-1.png" },
    { "src": "https://example.com/layer-2.png" }
  ]
}

version and slides are the only required fields. Everything else fills sensible defaults.

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description version 1 — Required. Must be the integer 1. slides Slide[] — Required. Ordered back-to-front: index 0 is farthest from camera. At least one slide. view "expanded" \| "compact" "expanded" Initial view to render. size { width, height } { width: 1920, height: 1080 } Plate pixel dimensions (controls the internal plate aspect ratio). background string (hex color) "#ffffff" Canvas background color. captions boolean true Global captions toggle. false removes all caption plates and lowers slide plates to the floor. camera Camera see below Camera / spacing settings. transition Transition | null null Animation settings. Needed by createStax with mode: "playable", and by transition() and toVideo() when no kind is passed. video Video see below Video export framing settings (overrides transition fps, adds holds). floor Floor see below Reflective floor plane. edge Edge { width: 0, color: "#f2f2f2" } Slide-plate border. caption_defaults CaptionStyle inherited from edge Default style for all captions. caption_fade CaptionFade see below Caption fade-in timing during transitions. juicy boolean false Per-channel colour match in the Python renderer; the browser renderer ignores it. $schema string — Optional, any string. The schema's $id is https://vexy.art/schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json; that address is an identifier and does not serve the file, so point your editor at the schema file itself.

docs.title: Slide
docs.text:
{
  "src": "layer-0.png",
  "gap": 960,
  "opacity": { "expanded": 1.0, "compact": 0.6 },
  "caption": {
    "text": "Halftone fill: Dots",
    "show_in": "expanded",
    "style": { "color": "#222222", "size": 48 }
  }
}
Field Type Default Description src string — Required. Path relative to the scene file, an absolute http(s) URL, or a data: URI. data: URIs carry base64-encoded image bytes inline — no network request, no URL resolution. gap number \| null null Per-slide gap override (scene-point units). null inherits camera.gap. opacity number \| { expanded, compact } 1.0 Slide opacity. A scalar stays constant; an object is interpolated during transitions. caption Caption | null null Optional caption plate below this slide.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
Controls spacing and the camera position for each view.

Field Type Default Description gap number 1920 Points between adjacent plates in the expanded view. distance number \| string "100%" Camera distance: an absolute scene-point value, or a viewport-fit percentage ("90%" = the deck fills 90% of the frame width). angle number 60 Azimuth degrees (horizontal orbit) for the expanded view. 0 = head-on. elevation number 0 Degrees above the horizon for the expanded view. fov number 39.6 Camera vertical field of view in degrees.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text:
{
  "kind": "expand_collapse",
  "duration": 3.0,
  "wait": 1.0,
  "fps": 30,
  "easing": "easeInOutCubic"
}
Field Type Default Description kind string — Required when transition is present. One of "expand", "collapse", "expand_collapse", "collapse_expand". duration number 3.0 Seconds per leg (e.g. one-way for expand; per-leg for expand_collapse). wait number 1.0 Hold seconds at the far-end endpoint between legs. fps integer 30 Frames per second for toVideo (overridden by video.fps when set). easing string "easeInOutCubic" Easing function: "linear", "easeInOutCubic", "easeOutCubic", or "easeInCubic".

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
Settings for video output. The browser's toVideo() reads fps, first_hold and last_hold; it records at the canvas size in real time, so it does not use frames, width or height; those are for the Python renderer.

Field Type Default Description fps integer transition.fps Output frames per second (overrides transition.fps). first_hold integer 10 Held copies of the start frame (still intro before the animation). last_hold integer 10 Held copies of the end frame (still outro after the animation). frames integer round(duration × fps) Transition frames per leg; omit to derive from timing. width integer size.width Output video width in pixels. height integer size.height Output video height in pixels.

docs.title: Floor
docs.text:
{ "color": "#f5f5f5", "opacity": 0.05, "reflectivity": 0.15 }
Field Type Default Description color string "#ffffff" Floor plane color. opacity number 0.0 Floor visibility (0 = invisible pane, faint reflections only). reflectivity number 0.1 Reflection strength [0,1].

docs.title: Edge
docs.text:
The visible border drawn around each slide plate.

Field Type Default Description width number 0.0 Border thickness as a fraction of plate height. 0 disables the border (and caption-plate borders). color string "#f2f2f2" Border color. Also the default fill_color and border_color for caption plates (overridable per caption).

docs.title: Caption
docs.text:
{
  "text": "Halftone fill: Dots",
  "show_in": "expanded",
  "style": {
    "size": 48,
    "color": "#222222",
    "font": "sans-serif",
    "fill_color": "#ffffff",
    "border_color": "#e0e0e0"
  }
}
Field Type Default Description text string — Required. Caption text. show_in "expanded" \| "compact" \| "both" \| "none" "expanded" Which view(s) display this caption plate. style CaptionStyle from caption_defaults Per-caption style overrides.

docs.title: CaptionStyle
docs.text:
Used in caption.style and caption_defaults.

Field Type Description size number Font size in scene-point units (1 em). color string Text color (hex). font string Font family name or path to a TrueType / OpenType font file. Falls back to system-ui, sans-serif. fill_color string Caption plate fill color. Defaults to edge.color. border_color string Caption plate border color. Defaults to edge.color.

docs.title: CaptionFade
docs.text:
Controls how captions fade in during a transition (back-to-front stagger).

Field Type Default Description window number 0.9 Fraction of the morph [0,1] (from the end) over which captions fade in. stagger number 0.3 Back→front succession spread as a fraction of the fade window. stagger_frames integer — Per-caption step in transition frames (overrides stagger when set).

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
{
  "$schema": "https://vexy.art/schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "view": "compact",
  "size": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080 },
  "background": "#f8f8f8",
  "captions": true,
  "camera": {
    "gap": 960,
    "distance": "90%",
    "angle": 55,
    "fov": 39.6
  },
  "transition": {
    "kind": "expand_collapse",
    "duration": 3.0,
    "wait": 1.0,
    "fps": 30,
    "easing": "easeInOutCubic"
  },
  "video": {
    "first_hold": 10,
    "last_hold": 10
  },
  "floor": { "color": "#ffffff", "opacity": 0.0, "reflectivity": 0.1 },
  "edge": { "width": 0.0, "color": "#f2f2f2" },
  "caption_defaults": { "size": 48, "color": "#333333", "font": "sans-serif" },
  "caption_fade": { "window": 0.9, "stagger": 0.3 },
  "slides": [
    {
      "src": "layer-0.png",
      "opacity": { "expanded": 1.0, "compact": 0.5 },
      "caption": { "text": "Background layer", "show_in": "expanded" }
    },
    {
      "src": "https://example.com/layer-1.png",
      "gap": 480,
      "caption": {
        "text": "Remote image — served with CORS",
        "show_in": "both",
        "style": { "color": "#0055aa" }
      }
    },
    {
      "src": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...",
      "caption": { "text": "Inline image — base64 data URI", "show_in": "expanded" }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Web Component
docs.text:
<vexy-stax> puts a deck on a page with markup only. Load the element bundle once; the element registers itself under the tag name vexy-stax.

<script type="module" src="https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.element.js"></script>

<!-- a deck from a list of images -->
<vexy-stax slides="layer-0.png layer-1.png layer-2.png"></vexy-stax>

<!-- a deck from a scene file -->
<vexy-stax scene="deck.scene.json" view="compact" aspect="16/9" buttons></vexy-stax>

The global bundle vexy-stax.global.js registers the same element.

docs.title: How the element mounts
docs.text:
When the element is added to the page, it:

  1. sets display: block and position: relative unless they are already set, and applies width, height and aspect;
  2. finds the scene, in this order of precedence:
    1. the config property or config attribute (an inline scene),
    2. a child <script type="application/json"> or <script type="application/vexy-scene+json"> (an inline scene),
    3. the scene attribute (a URL to fetch),
    4. the slides attribute (a list of image URLs);
  3. creates a VexyStax instance inside itself and waits until the textures are loaded;
  4. starts scroll tracking if mode="scrollspy";
  5. turns on click-to-toggle unless click-toggle="false";
  6. adds control buttons if buttons is present;
  7. fires ready.

If none of the four scene sources is present, the element renders nothing. Relative slide paths in an inline scene or in slides resolve against the page URL; in a scene file they resolve against the scene file's URL.

docs.title: Scene source
View and size
docs.text:
Attribute Value Default Effect view expanded or compact the scene's view, else expanded Initial view. Changing it later calls setView. width CSS length; a bare number means pixels — CSS width of the element height CSS length; a bare number means pixels — CSS height of the element aspect 3, 3/1, 3:1, 16x9, … — CSS aspect-ratio; : and x become /

The camera fits the deck to the element's box whenever its size changes.

docs.title: Playback mode
docs.text:
Attribute Value Default Effect mode static, playable or scrollspy static See below trigger CSS selector the element The element whose scroll position drives scrollspy
  • static renders the initial view.
  • playable also renders the initial view. The element does not start the transition itself; call el.transition() from your script, for example from a button or the ready event. (createStax with mode: "playable" does play the transition once.)
  • scrollspy maps the scroll position of the trigger to the morph between compact and expanded. See scrollspy.

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text:
Attribute Value Default Effect click-toggle false to turn off on A click inside the element animates to the other view buttons toggle, pair, or empty no buttons toggle: one button whose label follows the view. pair: two buttons. An empty buttons attribute means toggle. false means no buttons. explain-label text Explain Label of the button that expands the deck preview-label text Preview Label of the button that collapses the deck buttons-position bottom, top, bottom-left, bottom-right, top-left, top-right, center bottom Position of the buttons inside the element

Changing width, height, aspect, view or click-toggle updates the mounted deck in place. Changing any other observed attribute mounts the deck again.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Type Effect config object, JSON string or null Inline scene; setting it mounts the deck again scene string or object Setting an object, or a string that starts with {, sets config. Setting another string sets the scene attribute. Reading returns config, else the scene attribute. instance VexyStax or null The underlying instance, null until mounted

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
The element forwards these calls to its VexyStax instance. Before the instance exists they return undefined.

Method See setView(view) setView seek(t) seek transition(kind, opts) transition toggleView() toggleView toImage(opts) toImage toVideo(opts) toVideo scrollspy(opts) scrollspy

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
All events are CustomEvents dispatched on the element.

Event detail Fired when ready { instance } The deck is mounted and its first view is rendered error { error } Mounting failed, for example because the scene is invalid transitionstart { kind } A transition animation starts transitionend { kind } A transition animation finishes viewchange { view } The current view changes between compact and expanded, including when a scroll-driven seek crosses the halfway point 
const el = document.querySelector("vexy-stax");
el.addEventListener("ready", (e) => {
  e.detail.instance.transition("expand");
});

docs.title: Styling the buttons
docs.text:
The buttons read these CSS custom properties from the element:

Property Default --vexy-btn-color #000 --vexy-btn-bg rgba(0,0,0,0.05) --vexy-btn-blur 10px --vexy-btn-border 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.08) --vexy-btn-radius 999px --vexy-btn-pad 9px 18px --vexy-btn-font 14px (font size) --vexy-btn-weight 600 --vexy-btn-shadow 0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.06) --vexy-btn-bg-solid rgba(255,255,255,0.92) (Safari) --vexy-btn-bg-solid-hover rgba(255,255,255,0.97) (Safari, hover)

Safari ignores backdrop-filter over a canvas, so it uses the two -solid backgrounds instead of the blurred one.

vexy-stax {
  --vexy-btn-color: #fff;
  --vexy-btn-bg: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
  --vexy-btn-blur: 14px;
}

docs.title: Exports of the element bundle
docs.text:
vexy-stax.element.js is also an ES module. Besides registering the element, it exports VexyStax, createStax, makeScene, loadScene, parseScene and the element class VexyStaxElement:

import { createStax, makeScene } from "https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-js/vexy-stax.element.js";
